newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed out the week with a notable drop after some profit-taking in late trade that caused the spread over the German benchmark to widen to 169 from 161 bp earlier.

Traders said the market foundation remained solid, boosted by better than expected inflation data in both the U.S. and domestically, where September CPI rose 0.2 percent against a predicted 0.3 percent for a 3.6 percent year-on-year.
"To judge by fundamentals, the tendency should be upward," one trader said. "Perhaps what happened is that the bono has finished its autonomous route."

The general conviction among analysts was that the most difficult criteria to meet for joining Europe's single currency was going to be inflation, which meant there had to be a continued tight policy on rates.
They did not see the Bank of Spain cutting rates further despite the good inflation data.

The peseta closed near support levels against the mark, surprising dealers with its strength and sparking rumours of Bank of Spain intervention. "The firmness of the peseta is surprising at the close coinciding as it is with the big fall in bond futures," one dealer said.
